findings.title: Prompt rendering escapes the cap marker
findings.detail: The spec pre-renders `tests_touched` with `json.dumps(entries, indent=2, sort_keys=True)`. The default `ensure_ascii=True` turns the pinned marker `"… N more"` into `"… N more"` in the prompt. Non-ASCII test names would be escaped the same way. The Test plan pins the literal `"… N more"`, so a prompt-level check would fail or the reviewer would see an odd marker. Add `ensure_ascii=False` to the spec, or say the literal is only pinned on the returned list.

findings.title: Test-file rule contradicts the conftest/helper exclusion
findings.detail: A test file is defined as a `.py` file under `tests/` or matching `test_*.py` / `*_test.py`. The same paragraph says `conftest.py` helpers are skipped. A `tests/conftest.py` or `tests/helpers.py` satisfies the first rule, so the two statements conflict. The spec also doesn't say whether an entry with empty `changed` and `removed` is emitted (a `tests/` helper edit, or an R100 rename). AC3 says 'an R100 rename lists nothing as changed', which could mean either an entry with empty lists or no entry. Pin one behaviour, for example 'skip `conftest.py`; emit the entry with empty lists for an R100 rename', so the AC3 fixtures are unambiguous.

findings.title: Shell substitution in the merge-base description
findings.detail: `git show $(git merge-base <base> HEAD):<oldpath>` is shell syntax. The implementation will make two git calls, one for `merge-base` and one for `show <sha>:<path>`. Reword so nobody builds a `shell=True` call.

findings.title: AC1 only checks the template by substring
findings.detail: AC1 requires the template to 'contain the regression rule ... and the severity mapping', which a test can only check with substring or keyword assertions. That is fine for a prompt file, but name the exact phrases (for example `must_fix`, `removed`) so the test isn't a tautology.
